lead.headline: SEC opens secondary trading for tokenized equities, creating first regulated on-ramp for stocks on-chain
lead.tldr: U.S. regulators are bypassing legislative gridlock through exemptions to build a tokenized equity market structure; this week marks the first credible regulatory framework for 24/7 on-chain stock trading, while ZetaChain's vote to abandon its Layer 1 signals that infrastructure monetization remains brutally competitive.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week's signals show U.S. regulators constructing a tokenized equity market through exemptions rather than legislation, while infrastructure projects face hard choices about whether to own the stack or ride someone else's.

top_signals.title: It's here — SEC releases long-awaited innovation exemption to 'bring America's capital markets into the digital age'
top_signals.summary: The SEC has released a long-awaited 'innovation exemption' aimed at modernizing U.S. capital markets for the digital age. This move is positioned as a regulatory response to the lack of legislative progress in the Senate regarding crypto assets.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The SEC's innovation exemption reveals a regulatory strategy of bypassing a paralyzed Senate to create crypto market structure through administrative fiat, which introduces execution risk if political leadership changes but also accelerates the timeline for institutional product development.

top_signals.title: House committee moves to codify Trump's Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
top_signals.summary: A U.S. House committee has advanced legislation to establish a strategic bitcoin reserve. This move aims to codify the proposal for the United States to maintain permanent bitcoin holdings.
top_signals.why_it_matters: House codification of a strategic Bitcoin reserve would remove presidential discretion and create a permanent, non-discretionary buyer of last resort, repricing sovereign demand assumptions in Bitcoin valuation models.

top_signals.title: ZetaChain votes to shut down Layer 1 network and move ZETA to Solana
top_signals.summary: ZetaChain has initiated a vote to shut down its own Layer 1 network and migrate the ZETA token to the Solana blockchain. This represents a major strategic pivot from operating an independent chain to becoming a tokenized asset on an existing high-performance network.
top_signals.why_it_matters: ZetaChain's vote to shutter its Layer 1 and migrate to Solana is a data point on the terminal velocity of standalone chain economics: when sequencer revenue and validator incentives cannot sustain network effects, token value accrues faster to liquidity and distribution than to proprietary infrastructure.

top_signals.title: SEC Paves Way for Tokenized Stocks With Secondary Trading Exemption
top_signals.summary: The SEC has established a bounded pathway and secondary trading exemption to facilitate the launch of tokenized stocks. This approach allows the Commission to observe and improve market structures rather than applying outdated rules to new technology.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The SEC's secondary trading exemption for tokenized stocks creates a bounded experiment where the Commission can observe market structure evolution in real-time, reducing regulatory uncertainty for issuers willing to operate within transparency limits and trading caps.

top_signals.title: US regulator opens markets to tokenised stock trading
top_signals.summary: US regulators are moving toward allowing the trading of tokenized stocks, enabling blockchain-based representations of equities. This shift could allow for 24/7 trading and more efficient use of assets as collateral.
top_signals.why_it_matters: 24/7 tokenized stock trading and collateral efficiency represent a genuine use case for blockchain settlement that does not depend on crypto-native asset speculation, broadening the addressable market for on-chain infrastructure providers.

top_signals.title: SEC grants temporary exemption for tokenized US stock trading
top_signals.summary: The SEC has granted a temporary exemption allowing for the limited trading of tokenized US stocks on onchain venues. This move is subject to specific transparency rules and trading limits.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The temporary nature of this exemption means institutional capital deployment will remain cautious until permanence is established, creating a window for nimble operators to capture market share before incumbents commit.

deals.summary: S&P Global has agreed to acquire OpenZeppelin to strengthen its capabilities in onchain security. OpenZeppelin will maintain its operations as a standalone business unit following the acquisition.
Singapore-based stablecoin payments firm Dtcpay has completed its Series A funding round, totaling $25 million. The round saw the addition of SBI Group as a strategic investor.

Tare has raised $13 million in funding led by Blockchain Capital to develop a platform for managing private credit transactions on the blockchain. The startup aims to streamline credit operations to improve returns for both lenders and borrowers.
Exein has raised $270 million to develop tools to combat AI-driven hacking threats. The funding round has resulted in the company achieving unicorn status and doubling its valuation.

Fin.com has emerged from stealth with a $20 million seed round to develop global stablecoin infrastructure. The company focuses on providing the necessary tools for businesses to transition stablecoins into local bank accounts.

on_the_radar.title: 'Go time': SEC, CFTC prepare to push crypto rules as Clarity Act stalls in Senate
on_the_radar.summary: The SEC and CFTC are preparing to implement their own cryptocurrency regulations as the Clarity Act faces delays in the Senate. CFTC Chair Mike Selig indicated that the agency is ready to finalize and deploy rules for the digital asset sector.

on_the_radar.title: US House tax committee advances crypto tax overhaul in 38–5 voteA bipartisan House committee vote advanced legislation that would reshape federal tax rules for stablecoins, staking, crypto lending and digital asset transactions., US House tax committee advances crypto tax overhaul in 38–5 vote
on_the_radar.summary: A US House tax committee has passed a bipartisan bill in a 38–5 vote to overhaul federal tax rules for digital assets. The legislation aims to reshape how stablecoins, staking, and crypto lending are taxed.

on_the_radar.title: Circle launches Arc mainnet with BlackRock and Visa among validators, mints 10 billion ARC tokens
on_the_radar.summary: Circle has launched the Arc mainnet, featuring industry giants BlackRock and Visa as validators. The company has completed the genesis mint of 10 billion ARC tokens, though a public launch date is not yet determined.

on_the_radar.title: Deutsche Bank plans bitcoin, ether custody for institutional clients in Europe
on_the_radar.summary: Deutsche Bank is planning to launch a digital asset custody service for institutional clients in Europe later this year. The service will initially support Bitcoin, Ether, and specific stablecoins.

on_the_radar.title: Landmark US crypto bill fails as Senate splits over Trump ethics concerns
on_the_radar.summary: A landmark US cryptocurrency bill has failed to pass as the Senate remained divided over ethics concerns regarding Donald Trump. This represents a significant setback for the crypto industry following extensive lobbying efforts for a more favorable market structure.

on_the_radar.title: DOJ charges Robinhood engineers with front-running crypto listings on Hyperliquid
on_the_radar.summary: The US Department of Justice has charged two Robinhood engineers with front-running cryptocurrency listings. The individuals allegedly took positions in tokens on Hyperliquid before Robinhood's public listing announcements between 2025 and 2026.

on_the_radar.title: Balancer proposes winding down protocol and distributing treasury to BAL holders
on_the_radar.summary: Balancer is proposing to wind down its protocol and distribute its remaining treasury to BAL token holders. This follows the shutdown of Balancer Labs after a massive $128 million exploit in 2025.

on_the_radar.title: North Korean fake recruiters infect 30K devices, steal $10.7M in crypto
on_the_radar.summary: North Korean-linked threat actor WaterPlum used fake job recruitment schemes to infect 30,000 devices across 100 countries. The operation resulted in the compromise of over 7,000 crypto wallets and the theft of $10.7 million in digital assets.

on_the_radar.title: Bastion wins conditional OCC approval for national trust bank charter25m, Bastion wins conditional OCC approval for national trust bank charterBastion Platforms National Trust Company will offer stablecoin custody and wallets, payment infrastructure and white-label issuance from a single federally regulated entity.
on_the_radar.summary: Bastion Platforms has received conditional approval from the OCC for a national trust bank charter. This allows the company to provide federally regulated stablecoin custody, wallets, and payment infrastructure.

on_the_radar.title: Coinbase files to bring single-stock perpetual futures to US market23m, Coinbase files to bring single-stock perpetual futures to US marketCoinbase wants to bring 24/5 perpetual futures trading to individual US stocks, with its proposed contracts now awaiting regulatory approval.
on_the_radar.summary: Coinbase has filed for regulatory approval to introduce single-stock perpetual futures for the US market. This would allow users to trade individual stocks on a 24/5 basis using perpetual contracts.

on_the_radar.title: CFTC submits crypto market regulation plan for White House review
on_the_radar.summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has submitted a plan for new crypto market regulations to the White House for review. The agency intends to implement these rules using its existing regulatory authority.

on_the_radar.title: Banks double on EU MiCA crypto provider list as share hits 23%
on_the_radar.summary: The number of crypto service providers on ESMA's MiCA list has grown significantly, with banks increasing their market share of these providers to 23%. This indicates growing institutional adoption and regulatory alignment within the European Union.

worth_a_read.note: Exein's $270 million raise at doubled valuation is worth tracking as a benchmark for whether AI-security convergence narratives can sustain premium multiples in a tightening growth environment.

worth_a_read.title: Revolut mulls dual listing in London and New York
worth_a_read.note: Revolut's dual-listing deliberation offers a lens on how fintech incumbents are weighing regulatory arbitrage between London and New York, relevant for any crypto firm considering public market access.

worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's venture capital data provides context for whether this week's deal flow represents a genuine thaw or selective liquidity for proven founders in a market where Series A extension rounds remain more common than priced rounds.

linkedin_post:
The SEC did not wait for the Senate. Three exemptions in one week—innovation, tokenized stocks, secondary trading—built a market structure that does not exist in statute. This is administrative construction, not legislation, and the durability depends entirely on the 2026 election map.

We underwrite tokenized equity on whether 24/7 settlement and collateral efficiency justify the compliance cost of operating inside SEC guardrails. The temporary nature of the stock trading exemption keeps most institutional capital sidelined. That creates a window. Nimble issuers and infrastructure providers can capture distribution before Goldman or BlackRock commits engineering teams.

ZetaChain voting to kill its own Layer 1 and migrate ZETA to Solana is the other side of this. Infrastructure is not automatically valuable. When sequencer economics fail and validator incentives dry up, the token re-prices to liquidity and distribution, not proprietary stack ownership. We have seen this movie before. It usually ends with a small team maintaining a bridge contract.

The test: does any issuer actually launch tokenized equities under these caps and transparency rules before November 2026? If yes, the market structure hardens. If no, the exemptions expire and we are back to waiting for Senatorial courage.

We are underwriting for the former. Cautiously.
